players.product: dimensional & materials metrology for leading-edge nodes

quarterly_data.signal: RECORD Q2 2026 revenue of $255 million, at the high end of guidance and Nova's first quarter above $250 million, up 8% quarter-over-quarter and 16% year-over-year. Gross margin 57% GAAP / 58% non-GAAP; operating expenses $68 million GAAP / $62.9 million non-GAAP; operating margin 30% GAAP / 33% non-GAAP, at the upper end of the 28%-33% target model; effective tax rate approximately 16%; EPS $2.20 GAAP and a record $2.51 non-GAAP, exceeding the high end of guidance. Product revenue split approximately 73% logic and foundry / 27% memory and others. Two customers and four territories each contributed 10% or more of product revenue. Cash and investments of more than $1.7 billion fund R&D, growth initiatives and selective M&A. Demand was broad-based, with record sales in multiple product lines and services led by advanced logic and advanced packaging.
quarterly_data.figure: Record revenue $255M (+8% QoQ, +16% YoY); non-GAAP GM 58%, op margin 33%, EPS $2.51; mix 73% logic/foundry vs 27% memory; cash >$1.7B

quarterly_data.signal: Q3 2026 guidance: revenue $277-$287 million (another record, and roughly +10% sequentially at the midpoint - a figure computed from the $255 million Q2 base, not stated on the call), GAAP EPS $2.46-$2.61 and non-GAAP EPS $2.70-$2.85. At the midpoint: gross margin approximately 57% GAAP / 59% non-GAAP, operating expenses approximately $74 million GAAP / $68 million non-GAAP, effective tax rate approximately 17%. First-half 2026 gross margin was approximately 59% and management expects FULL-YEAR gross margin of approximately 59%, with the 57%-60% target gross-margin model 'well intact.' Nova expects to deliver ANOTHER YEAR OF DOUBLE-DIGIT GROWTH in 2026 and believes it is on a path to reach its organic growth objectives SOONER THAN ORIGINALLY PLANNED; the next long-term strategic plan will be presented at an INVESTOR DAY IN Q1 2027.
quarterly_data.figure: Q3 guide $277M-$287M revenue, non-GAAP EPS $2.70-$2.85, non-GAAP GM ~59%; full-year GM ~59%; 57%-60% target GM model intact

quarterly_data.signal: Revenue associated with ADVANCED LOGIC MORE THAN DOUBLED SEQUENTIALLY in Q2 as customers expanded production capacity, with demand stretching across product lines and divisions. The VeraFlex XPS materials-metrology platform kept gaining traction, driven by 'proliferation in gate-all-around manufacturers' as customers continue to INCREASE THE NUMBER OF VERAFLEX TOOLS PER FAB; XPS adoption is rising in logic, especially at the advanced nodes. Nova's AI-enabling modeling solution, combining physics-based and machine-learning algorithms, helps customers address the complex 3D device structures of gate-all-around and plays an increasingly important role in managing Nova's expanding GAA install base. An analyst characterised Nova as holding a position across ALL FOUR gate-all-around players and management did not dispute it, while declining to discuss any customer by name.
quarterly_data.figure: Advanced logic revenue more than doubled QoQ; VeraFlex tools per fab increasing at gate-all-around manufacturers; logic and foundry 73% of Q2 product revenue

quarterly_data.signal: ADVANCED PACKAGING set a record and contributed nearly one-quarter - 'nearing 25%' - of overall product revenue in Q2, driven by the dimensional metrology portfolio and fuelled by customers' continued investment in advanced packaging and HIGH-BANDWIDTH MEMORY capacity to support AI-related device demand. Nova had guided advanced packaging to between 20 and 25% of product revenue for the year and now sees it 'inching towards the 25% for the year.' Management frames advanced packaging as a MULTI-YEAR STRUCTURAL growth opportunity that has gone from essentially no revenue several years ago to a meaningful contributor, now spanning optical, chemical AND materials metrology, and becoming increasingly similar to front-end manufacturing in complexity across both logic and memory. Chiplets, HYBRID BONDING, PANEL-LEVEL PACKAGING and 2.5D integration all increase both the number of measurements required and their criticality; hybrid bonding is described as 'an additional layer that will accelerate this growth for Nova.'
quarterly_data.figure: Advanced packaging a record at nearly 25% of Q2 product revenue, inching toward 25% for the full year (initially guided 20-25%)

quarterly_data.signal: The Nova WMC dimensional-metrology platform won a recent TOOL OF RECORD SELECTION BY A LEADING FOUNDRY CUSTOMER (not named on the call) for MULTIPLE LAYERS MEASUREMENT in advanced-packaging production flows. Nova is also seeing accelerating WMC adoption across BOTH memory and foundry customers, 'positioning us to benefit from further investment in advanced packaging and high-bandwidth memory manufacturing.' A new configuration of the Nova WMC extends its dimensional metrology capabilities to PANEL-LEVEL PACKAGING.

Memory and others was 27% of Q2 product revenue and Nova projects MEMORY AT ABOUT 30% for full-year 2026, a slight increase on the 70/30 logic-to-memory ratio of 2025, against a long-term model of about 60/40 in favour of logic because process-control intensity in logic is higher. The MAJORITY OF NOVA'S MEMORY EXPOSURE IS DRAM, where demand is strong, while 3D NAND remains 'somehow muted' this year because its growth is driven by UPGRADES rather than capacity expansion - even though metrology intensity between DRAM and NAND is 'more or less similar.' Nova sells to ALL THE TOP PLAYERS IN THE NAND MARKET (positions vary by product line) and expects to benefit once NAND capacity investment returns, which management hopes will be sometime next year. Coming DRAM technology transitions - 4F-squared, 6F-squared, advanced DRAM architectures and eventually 3D DRAM - all increase process complexity and metrology requirements. A new generation of the Nova PRISM platform is targeted at advanced memory structures.
quarterly_data.figure: Memory 27% of Q2 product revenue and ~30% expected for 2026 (2025 was 70/30); long-term model 60/40 logic/memory; DRAM strong, 3D NAND muted and upgrade-driven

quarterly_data.signal: VISIBILITY IS 'UNPRECEDENTED' versus prior cycles because demand is coming from logic AND memory at the same time: customers are planning further ahead and giving Nova longer-term visibility into next year so that committed lead times can be met - something management says did not happen in previous cycles, long or short. In some cases Nova is ALREADY RECEIVING ORDERS AND PLANNING 2027 DELIVERIES, and customer PULL-INS drove the first half and are driving the second half of 2026. Asked to endorse buy-side / sell-side talk of 40% WFE growth in 2027 (implying $210 billion-$215 billion), management said it is TOO EARLY to say whether 2027 grows 40%, but that it does anticipate 2027 to be a GROWTH YEAR for Nova and is working to ensure its supply chain can provide the needed capacity. Management also called the demand drivers 'increasingly durable in nature,' with enhanced visibility into the remainder of 2026 and into 2027.
quarterly_data.figure: 2027 orders already being received and deliveries planned; management would not endorse the 40% 2027 WFE growth / $210B-$215B scenario put to it

quarterly_data.signal: Nova's SUPPLY CHAIN IS STRETCHED and management is actively managing both production and suppliers to hold lead times as orders increase. LEAD TIMES ARE FOUR TO 12 MONTHS AT THE LATEST depending on the product line - essentially unchanged versus the prior three months and described as best-in-class for the industry. On capacity, Nova completed a CLEAN ROOM EXPANSION IN CALIFORNIA THAT DOUBLES ITS U.S. MANUFACTURING CAPACITY, a step driven in part by VeraFlex XPS traction at gate-all-around customers. On input costs, higher MEMORY COMPONENT PRICES do affect Nova's BOM, but the memory portion of the BOM is 'not significant,' so management sees no major change to its gross-margin profile; ASPs are being balanced against long-term customer relationships rather than repriced opportunistically, and the gross-margin model is expected to hold through this year and next.
quarterly_data.figure: Lead times four to 12 months depending on product line; California clean room expansion doubles U.S. manufacturing capacity; memory BOM inflation not significant to gross margin

quarterly_data.signal: Product introductions this quarter: a NEW GENERATION OF NOVA PRISM targeted at advanced memory structures, a NEW GENERATION OF NOVA VERAFLEX for materials metrology, a NEW CONFIGURATION OF NOVA WMC extending dimensional metrology to panel-level packaging, and NOVAHUB - a scalable software platform for fleet and AI-driven analytics that supports the efficient operation of large metrology fleets. Nova ancosys front-end chemical metrology posted RECORD SALES on both advanced memory and mature logic applications, with continued market share gains at the front end of the line (an analyst noted the release also called out a record in Sentronics). The 'lab-to-fab' products METRION and ELIPSON have moved into HIGH-VOLUME MANUFACTURING PROLIFERATION, with Metrion adoption continuing to accelerate across both logic and memory customers on more qualifications and higher tool utilisation; the stated goal is to replicate the XPS model of MULTIPLE TOOLS PER FAB. SERVICE REVENUE reached another record, augmented by value-added services and customer upgrades of installed tools to address new process requirements and chemistries. Nova invests approximately 15% of revenue in R&D.
quarterly_data.figure: Record ancosys and record service revenue; new PRISM, VeraFlex and panel-level WMC configurations plus NovaHub software; Metrion and ELIPSON in high-volume manufacturing proliferation; R&D approximately 15% of revenue

quarterly_data.signal: On PROCESS-CONTROL INTENSITY, management said it has to be broken down by end market because each behaves differently: LOGIC INTENSITY IS HIGHER THAN MEMORY, ADVANCED PACKAGING IS 'RAPIDLY GROWING,' and 3D NAND is currently muted in process control because its spend is upgrades rather than capacity expansion. Asked about the Terafab greenfield project, management declined to comment on any specific customer but said generically that PROCESS CONTROL INTENSITY AT THE INITIAL STAGES OF GREENFIELD FABS IS HIGHER THAN IN THE ONGOING OPERATIONS OF MORE MATURE FABS, because a new fab operator must improve time to market and reach the required yield threshold - citing the Rapidus build of a couple of years ago as an example of that pattern rather than as a Nova customer statement. The structural drivers - increasing complexity in architectures and materials - remain in place, and Nova points to customer adoption, market share gains and technology wins as its key indicators of outperformance.
